subject: Archaeology
title: The Minoan Collapse
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Minoan Collapse.

hook.text: Europe's first great civilization — the Minoans of Crete — built grand palaces and then vanished around 1450 BCE.

buildup.text: The Minoans had flushing toilets, multi-story buildings, and vibrant art. They dominated the Aegean for over 500 years.

discovery.text: The volcanic eruption of Thera around 1600 BCE devastated the region.

twist.text: The final destruction came 150 years after Thera — meaning the eruption weakened them but something else delivered the fatal blow.

climax.text: Mycenaean Greeks from the mainland took over Crete around 1450 BCE.

punchline.text: A volcano weakened them. Greeks finished them.

quiz.question: What likely caused the final end of Minoan civilization?
options: The Thera eruption destroyed all their palaces in a single day
Mycenaean Greeks conquered Crete about 150 years after the Thera eruption
A plague carried by Egyptian traders wiped out the population
